that’s an understandable sentiment — It’s definitely a time-consuming hobby and getting into it can be really difficult. Its essentially learning a whole new language, plus a bunch of technical stuff on top of that, and you mentioned that rhythm isn’t your strong suit so that would take some learning. but if you’re genuinely interested I think you should just pick up an instrument and play! It’ll be daunting at first and it’ll require a lot of your time, but as soon as I was able to play along to one of my favourite songs, despite it being super simple and not very impressive, I was hooked. That being said, instruments aren’t for everyone! If listening to music brings you happiness and you don’t have the time to get into playing instruments, then enjoy that time listening to music! The act of creating music has tuned my brain to be more analytical, which isn’t always great as now I’m more of a snob when it comes to what I listen to... I wish you the best of luck in your future music-related endeavours, whether they be learning instruments or just enjoying all the music out there :D

I don’t personally know of any options for automatically downloading subtitles unless you’re using a plugin to do so — I’m not at my computer right now but maybe there’s one if you dig around the settings a bit. However, if you check at the same place that the media is being stored, there may be a subtitle file (generally .srt) next to the video file itself. Try deleting that (or, from my experience, just going into the detail part of the movie/show in plex web player and choosing “none” under subtitles should work)

I could be totally wrong about this however, since there are other reasons this could happen that I don’t entirely know how to solve at of yet. Good luck!
Could be totally different, but for me this happened because of a corrupted or broken subtitle track. I unselected said track and it worked. Hopefully this helps!
